mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs compressing equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the rate hike, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor market participation reduces risk aversion.
regime_hint: High unemployment and rising wage pressure
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days after the trigger, or the effect reverses in the next 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (household spending index) exceeds 575 by more than 10 points, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive as stronger consumer demand boosts corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 20-day window, or the effect persists only in non-cyclical months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5 points coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing output signals economic weakness and lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the production decline, or the effect is not robust across multiple quarters.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by at least 0.2 percentage points each are associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as dual signals of disinflation and policy easing.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev and CPIAUCSL < prev by ≥0.2%
regime_hint: Double-dip inflation and rate cut anticipation
failure_condition: No significant return in 60 days, or the interaction is not statistically detectable (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) by 2,000 or more in a month is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market stress raises risk aversion.
failure_condition: Return is positive despite the employment decline, or the effect is only observed in non-crisis months.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (GDP chained) exceeds 13150 by at least 2% from the prior quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive as strong quarterly growth boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days, or the effect is absent in high-inflation quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month declining trend in RSAFS (real S&P 500 adjusted futures) with a monthly drop of at least 5,000 points predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market expectations of further declines in equities dominate.
candidate_trigger: 3-month downward trend in RSAFS with monthly drop ≥5,000
failure_condition: Forward returns are positive despite the trend, or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
